subject: Franska 3
title: Expressing and justifying an opinion
sourceSummary: Vocabulary and phrases for giving your opinion, agreeing or disagreeing, and justifying what you think.

questions.prompt: Which phrase expresses an opinion in French?
questions.opener: A common way to open with what you think.
questions.explanation: "À mon avis" means "in my opinion" and is used to introduce an opinion: "À mon avis, ce film est excellent."

questions.prompt: What does "Je pense que le recyclage devrait être obligatoire" mean?
questions.opener: "Je pense que" followed by a statement.
choices: I think recycling should be mandatory
I'm asking whether recycling is mandatory
questions.explanation: "Je pense que" means "I think that", and "devrait être obligatoire" means "should be mandatory".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrase to AGREE with someone: "Nous devrions manger moins de viande." — "Oui, ___ !"
questions.explanation: "Je suis d'accord" means "I agree". "Je ne suis pas d'accord" would mean the opposite.

questions.prompt: What does "Je ne suis pas du tout d'accord avec cette idée" mean?
choices: I partly agree with the idea
I completely disagree with the idea
questions.explanation: "Pas du tout" means "not at all", so "je ne suis pas du tout d'accord" means "I completely disagree".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct connector to justify an opinion: "Je pense qu'on devrait interdire les sacs plastique, ___ ils polluent les océans."
questions.opener: Which word links an opinion to its reason?
questions.explanation: "Parce que" (because) introduces the reason for the opinion. "Cependant" and "pourtant" both mean "however/yet", and "d'ailleurs" means "besides/by the way" — the wrong kind of connector here.

questions.prompt: What does "En revanche, certains pensent que c'est aux gouvernements d'agir, pas aux individus" express?
questions.opener: "En revanche" marks a contrast between opinions.
choices: A reinforcement of the previous opinion
A summary of everything said so far
questions.explanation: "En revanche" means "on the other hand" and introduces a counterargument or a contrasting opinion — common in argumentative texts.

questions.prompt: Write a short argumentative sentence (opinion + reason) about school meals, using the building blocks: "à mon avis", "parce que", "les repas scolaires", "sain(e)" (healthy).
questions.opener: Structure: opinion (à mon avis + statement) + reason (parce que + justification).
questions.answer: À mon avis, les repas scolaires devraient être plus sains, parce que les élèves ont besoin d'énergie pour bien apprendre.
steps: Start with the opinion phrase "à mon avis" followed by the statement: "les repas scolaires devraient être plus sains" (school meals should be healthier).
Add the reason with "parce que": "parce que les élèves ont besoin d'énergie pour bien apprendre" (because students need energy to learn well).
The full sentence combines opinion + justification, which is the basic structure of all argumentative writing: statement, then "parce que" + reason.
Other valid answers with the same structure (for example, a different reason) are also acceptable — what matters is that both the opinion and the reason are present and logically connected.

questions.prompt: What phrases do you need to express and justify an opinion in French?
questions.opener: Saying what you think, agreeing/disagreeing, and justifying why.
questions.answer: Expressing an opinion: à mon avis = in my opinion · je pense que / je trouve que / je crois que = I think that · selon moi = according to me. Agreeing: je suis d'accord (avec) = I agree (with) · tu as raison = you're right · exactement = exactly. Disagreeing: je ne suis pas d'accord = I disagree · je ne pense pas que... = I don't think that... · pas du tout = not at all. Justifying: parce que = because · car = for/because (written) · c'est pourquoi = that's why · en revanche / cependant / pourtant = on the other hand/however (for counterarguments).
